tagline: From the Niobrara bridges across the Sandhills to the buttes.
intro: US 20 leaves Valentine and its high bridges and heads west along Minnechaduza Creek, across the rolling Sandhills through Kilgore, Cody and Merriman, then over the wild prairie of the northern Panhandle by Gordon, Rushville and Chadron. Past Crawford it runs among bluffs and escarpments by the Red Cloud Buttes and on to Harrison and the Wyoming line, 197 miles in all.
Cody, along the way, was named for a railroad foreman and not for Buffalo Bill. Harrison, near the end, stands at 4,876 feet, the highest town in Nebraska, and bills itself as Nebraska's Top Town.

moments.title: Bryan Bridge
moments.text: Just south of Valentine stands a pin-connected steel arch of 1932 over the Niobrara, the only one of its kind in Nebraska, chosen by its designer because it blended into its surroundings.

moments.title: Toadstool Geologic Park
moments.text: North of Crawford, a one-mile loop trail winds through badlands of rock forms shaped like toadstools, past fossils that must stay where they lie.

moments.title: Fort Robinson
moments.text: Crazy Horse surrendered here with 1,100 followers in May 1877, and that September he was fatally wounded at the guardhouse door while resisting imprisonment.
